data.G: No integrated candidate yet; the supplied source is the baseline. After research, integrate only correctly validated candidates, then independently measure and confirm the actual combined G. Do not assume individual gains add.
data.analysis: Choose N=3 for distinct opportunities: improve the block-local reduction, reduce the ordinary multi-kernel hierarchy, and test a cooperative single-launch design. These target different costs and can be compared without assuming their gains combine. The supplied baseline is valid and measures 46.244 μs on average across three repeats. For n=2^22, the source computes four reduction stages (32,768 → 256 → 2 → 1 blocks), followed by a device-to-device copy. This identifies a plausible launch and reduction-kernel opportunity, but no profiling data establishes which dominates. The CUDA 12.6.3 Programming Guide documents grid synchronization with cooperative launch; actual GH200 runtime support and performance still need candidate validation. Preserve correctness for every valid input and all scratch/output constraints.

children.objective: Using AB-MCTS, optimize only the block-local reduction mechanism in src/candidate.cu: replace the current modulo/shared-memory tree with a warp-first reduction and one cross-warp combine, while keeping the existing 128-element block tile and recursive host reduction structure to isolate this change. Preserve correct tail handling, all valid n values, exact results, and scratch bounds. Report failed attempts and repeated full-program timings after correctness checks.
children.subject: Warp-first block reduction

children.objective: Using AB-MCTS, optimize the conventional multi-kernel reduction hierarchy in src/candidate.cu. Explore a coarse first-stage tile and a final pass that reduces its partials directly to output, aiming to reduce the large-input path from four reduction launches to two without relying on initialized scratch. Handle small inputs and tails generally; preserve the ABI, default stream, exact result, and scratch limits. Use permitted CUDA/CUB block primitives as appropriate, and report failed attempts plus repeated full correctness-checked timings.
children.subject: Fewer launches with a two-pass hierarchy

children.objective: Using AB-MCTS, investigate a single cooperative kernel in src/candidate.cu: each resident CTA computes a grid-stride partial, then a grid-wide synchronization lets one CTA produce the final output. Use the cooperative launch API and a grid size safe for residency; do not rely on an atomic counter or uninitialized scratch. Validate the launch path and correctness for every valid n. If unsupported, incorrect, or slower, record that result rather than assuming a gain; report repeated full-program timings.
children.subject: Single-launch cooperative reduction
